items.q: What skills should a Java developer have?
items.a: Java developer (backend) key skills: Core Java (OOP, collections, multithreading, Java 8+ features like streams and lambdas), Spring Boot, Spring MVC / Spring Data / Spring Security, REST APIs, Microservices, Hibernate / JPA, SQL databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle), Maven / Gradle, Git, unit testing (JUnit, Mockito). Good to have: Kafka / RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS / Azure, Redis, CI/CD (Jenkins). Common titles: Java Developer, Backend Engineer, Software Engineer (Java), Java Full Stack Developer.

items.q: Screening questions for a Java developer
also: java developer se kya poochna hai
items.a: Recruiter screening questions for Java: 1. Which Java version do you use and which Java 8+ features have you used? 2. Have you built REST APIs with Spring Boot? Explain one project. 3. Have you worked on microservices? How did services talk to each other (REST, Kafka)? 4. Which database did you use, and did you write queries yourself? 5. Which cloud or Docker / Kubernetes experience do you have? 6. What was your exact role: development, support or both? 7. Team size and how you deploy code (CI/CD)? Real hands-on answers with project details are a good sign.

items.q: Boolean search string for Java developer
items.a: Java developer Boolean string: ("Java Developer" OR "Java Engineer" OR "Backend Developer" OR "Software Engineer") AND ("Spring Boot" OR Spring) AND (Microservices OR "REST API") AND (Hibernate OR JPA) NOT (Intern OR Fresher OR Trainee). Add (AWS OR Kafka OR Docker) for senior roles.

items.q: What skills should a Python developer have?
items.a: Python developer key skills: core Python (OOP, data structures, exceptions, virtual environments), a web framework (Django, Flask or FastAPI), REST APIs, SQL and ORM (Django ORM, SQLAlchemy), NoSQL (MongoDB, Redis), Git, unit testing (pytest), Linux basics. Good to have: Celery, Docker, AWS / GCP, async programming, Pandas / NumPy (for data work). Check whether the candidate is web-focused (Django / FastAPI) or data-focused (Pandas, ML), since these are different roles.

items.q: Screening questions for a Python developer
also: python developer se kya poochna hai
items.a: Python screening questions: 1. Which framework do you use most: Django, Flask or FastAPI? 2. Describe an API or module you built yourself. 3. Which databases have you used with Python? 4. Have you deployed applications (Docker, AWS, Linux servers)? 5. Have you written unit tests (pytest)? 6. Any experience with Celery, async or background jobs? 7. Is your work more web development or data / automation scripts?

items.q: What skills should a React / frontend developer have?
items.a: Frontend (React) developer skills: HTML5, CSS3 (Flexbox, Grid, responsive design), JavaScript ES6+, TypeScript, React.js (hooks, components, state management with Redux / Zustand / Context), REST API integration, Git, browser dev tools. Good to have: Next.js, Tailwind / Material UI, testing (Jest, React Testing Library), performance optimisation, Webpack / Vite. Angular developers need Angular, TypeScript, RxJS and NgRx instead of React. Ask for a portfolio or GitHub link.

items.q: Screening questions for a React developer
also: react developer se kya poochna hai
items.a: React screening questions: 1. Which React version and hooks do you use regularly? 2. How do you manage state in a large app (Redux, Context, others)? 3. Do you use TypeScript? 4. Have you used Next.js or server-side rendering? 5. How do you make a page responsive? 6. Have you integrated REST or GraphQL APIs? 7. Can you share a live project or GitHub link?

items.q: What skills should a Node.js developer have?
items.a: Node.js developer skills: JavaScript / TypeScript, Node.js, Express.js or NestJS, REST APIs, async programming (promises, async/await), MongoDB or SQL databases, authentication (JWT, OAuth), Git. Good to have: Redis, message queues, Docker, AWS (Lambda, EC2, S3), GraphQL, socket.io, testing (Jest, Mocha). MERN stack = MongoDB, Express, React, Node; MEAN stack uses Angular instead of React.

items.q: What is a full stack developer?
also: full stack developer kya hota hai
items.a: A full stack developer works on both frontend (what the user sees: React, Angular, HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and backend (server, APIs and database: Node.js, Java, Python, .NET with SQL / MongoDB). Common stacks: MERN (MongoDB, Express, React, Node), MEAN (Angular instead of React), Java + React / Angular, Python (Django) + React, .NET + Angular. Always confirm which stack the client means and the split (e.g. 70 percent backend, 30 percent frontend).

items.q: What skills should a .NET developer have?
items.a: .NET developer skills: C#, .NET Core / .NET 6+, ASP.NET MVC and Web API, Entity Framework, LINQ, SQL Server (queries, stored procedures), REST APIs, Git. Good to have: Azure (App Services, Functions, DevOps), microservices, Angular or React for full stack roles, unit testing (xUnit, NUnit). Note: older .NET Framework (4.x) experience is different from modern .NET Core; check which one the client needs.

items.q: What skills should a PHP developer have?
items.a: PHP developer skills: PHP 7 / 8, OOP, Laravel (most common) or CodeIgniter / Symfony, MySQL, REST APIs, HTML, CSS, JavaScript / jQuery, Git. WordPress developers need theme and plugin development, custom post types and WooCommerce. Good to have: Vue.js or React, AWS, Docker, payment gateway integration.

items.q: What skills should an Android developer have?
items.a: Android developer skills: Kotlin (preferred) and Java, Android SDK, Jetpack components (ViewModel, LiveData, Room, Navigation), Jetpack Compose, MVVM architecture, REST API integration (Retrofit), coroutines, Firebase, Git, publishing on the Play Store. Good to have: dependency injection (Hilt / Dagger), unit testing, CI/CD for mobile. Ask for Play Store app links.

items.q: What skills should an iOS developer have?
items.a: iOS developer skills: Swift, SwiftUI and UIKit, Xcode, MVVM / MVC, Core Data, REST APIs (URLSession, Alamofire), Combine or async/await, push notifications, App Store publishing. Good to have: Objective-C (older apps), unit testing (XCTest), CI/CD (Fastlane). Ask for App Store app links.

items.q: Flutter vs React Native: what is the difference?
also: flutter aur react native me fark
items.a: Flutter and React Native are cross-platform frameworks: one codebase builds both Android and iOS apps. Flutter uses the Dart language (skills: Dart, widgets, state management with Provider / Bloc / Riverpod, Firebase, REST APIs). React Native uses JavaScript / TypeScript and React (skills: React, Redux, native modules, Expo). Ask for published app links and whether they have handled native integrations.

items.q: What skills should a DevOps engineer have?
items.a: DevOps engineer skills: Linux administration, scripting (Bash, Python), Git, CI/CD tools (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps), Docker, Kubernetes, cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, CloudFormation, Ansible), monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, CloudWatch), networking basics. DevOps engineers automate how code is built, tested, deployed and monitored. Related titles: SRE (Site Reliability Engineer), Cloud Engineer, Platform Engineer.

items.q: Screening questions for a DevOps engineer
also: devops engineer se kya poochna hai
items.a: DevOps screening questions: 1. Which cloud do you use (AWS / Azure / GCP) and which services? 2. Describe a CI/CD pipeline you built: tools and stages. 3. Have you managed Kubernetes clusters in production (EKS, AKS, GKE)? 4. Which Infrastructure as Code tool do you use (Terraform, Ansible)? 5. How do you monitor and handle incidents? 6. Any certifications (AWS Solutions Architect, CKA)? 7. Are you on call or doing 24x7 support?

items.q: What skills does a cloud engineer need?
items.a: Cloud engineer skills: one main cloud in depth. AWS: EC2, S3, VPC, IAM, RDS, Lambda, CloudFormation, EKS. Azure: VMs, Storage, VNet, Entra ID (Azure AD), AKS, App Services, ARM / Bicep. GCP: Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Storage, IAM. Plus Linux, networking (DNS, load balancers, subnets), security, Terraform, scripting and cost optimisation. Certifications (AWS Certified Solutions Architect, Azure AZ-104 / AZ-305) are valued. Cloud architects also design multi-service solutions.

items.q: What skills should a data engineer have?
items.a: Data engineer skills: SQL (advanced), Python or Scala, data pipelines / ETL, Apache Spark (PySpark), data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Synapse), orchestration (Airflow, ADF), cloud data services (AWS Glue, Azure Data Factory, Databricks), Kafka for streaming, data modelling. Data engineers build the systems that move and prepare data; data analysts and scientists then use that data.

items.q: What skills should a data analyst have?
items.a: Data analyst skills: Excel (advanced: pivots, VLOOKUP / XLOOKUP), SQL, a BI tool (Power BI with DAX, or Tableau), basic statistics, Python or R (Pandas) for analysis, data cleaning, dashboard design and presenting insights to business teams. Power BI / BI developers focus more on data models, DAX and building dashboards.

items.q: What skills should a data scientist / ML engineer have?
items.a: Data scientist skills: Python, statistics and probability, Pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, machine learning algorithms (regression, classification, clustering), model evaluation, SQL, data visualisation. ML / AI engineers also need deep learning (PyTorch, TensorFlow), deploying models (MLOps: Docker, MLflow, cloud ML services), and for GenAI roles: LLMs, prompt engineering, RAG, vector databases, LangChain / LlamaIndex, OpenAI / Anthropic APIs. Ask what models they built and whether they went to production.

items.q: What are the types of QA / testing roles?
items.a:
QA (Quality Assurance) / testing roles:
1. Manual tester: writes test cases and tests the application by hand (functional, regression, UAT).
2. Automation tester / QA automation engineer: writes code that tests automatically (Selenium, Cypress, Playwright, Appium).
3. SDET (Software Development Engineer in Test): strong coding plus testing; builds test frameworks and tooling.
4. Performance tester: load and stress testing (JMeter, LoadRunner, Gatling).
5. API tester: tests APIs (Postman, Rest Assured).
6. Mobile tester: Android / iOS apps (Appium).
7. Security tester: vulnerability and penetration testing.
8. QA lead / test manager: plans testing, manages the team and quality reports.

items.q: What skills should a manual tester have?
items.a: Manual tester skills: SDLC and STLC knowledge, writing test scenarios and test cases, test types (functional, regression, smoke, sanity, integration, UAT), bug reporting and life cycle, tools like JIRA / Azure DevOps, TestRail / Zephyr, basic SQL for data checks, API testing with Postman, Agile / Scrum. Good to have: basic automation knowledge, mobile testing, domain knowledge (banking, healthcare, e-commerce).

items.q: What skills should an automation tester have?
items.a: Automation tester skills: a programming language (Java most common, or Python / JavaScript / C#), Selenium WebDriver, a test framework (TestNG, JUnit, PyTest), framework design (Page Object Model, data-driven, hybrid), BDD (Cucumber, Gherkin), API automation (Rest Assured, Postman / Newman), Git, Maven, CI/CD integration (Jenkins), reporting (Extent Reports, Allure). Modern alternatives: Cypress, Playwright (JavaScript / TypeScript). Mobile: Appium. SDETs need stronger coding (data structures, design) as well.

items.q: Screening questions for a QA automation tester
also: automation tester se kya poochna hai
items.a: QA automation screening questions: 1. Which tool and language do you use (Selenium with Java, Cypress, Playwright)? 2. Did you build the automation framework yourself or maintain an existing one? Which design (POM, BDD)? 3. What percentage of your work is automation vs manual? 4. Have you done API testing or API automation (Postman, Rest Assured)? 5. How are your tests run in CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions)? 6. Which bug tracking and test management tools do you use? 7. Any mobile (Appium) or performance (JMeter) testing? Many "automation" profiles are mostly manual; ask for the real split.

items.q: Boolean search string for QA automation
items.a: QA automation Boolean string: ("Automation Tester" OR "QA Automation" OR "SDET" OR "Test Automation Engineer" OR "QA Engineer") AND (Selenium OR Cypress OR Playwright) AND (Java OR Python OR JavaScript) AND (TestNG OR Cucumber OR BDD OR "Rest Assured") NOT ("Manual Testing only" OR Intern). For manual QA: ("Manual Tester" OR "QA Analyst" OR "Test Engineer") AND ("Test Cases" OR "Functional Testing") AND (JIRA OR "Regression Testing").

items.q: What skills should a performance tester have?
items.a: Performance tester skills: JMeter (most common), LoadRunner, Gatling or k6; designing load, stress, spike and endurance tests; scripting and correlation; analysing response time, throughput and errors; monitoring servers (CPU, memory, DB) with APM tools (Dynatrace, AppDynamics, New Relic, Grafana); finding bottlenecks and reporting results.

items.q: What skills should a business analyst have?
items.a: IT business analyst skills: requirement gathering and stakeholder management, writing BRD / FRD documents and user stories with acceptance criteria, process flow diagrams (Visio, Lucidchart, BPMN), wireframes (Figma, Balsamiq), Agile / Scrum, JIRA / Confluence, SQL basics, UAT support, and domain knowledge (BFSI, healthcare, e-commerce, etc.). Certifications: CBAP, CCBA, PMI-PBA.

items.q: What is a Scrum Master and Project Manager?
items.a: Scrum Master: helps an Agile team follow Scrum, runs ceremonies (daily stand-up, sprint planning, review, retrospective), removes blockers; certifications CSM or PSM. Project Manager: owns scope, timeline, budget, risks and client communication; certifications PMP or PRINCE2. Product Owner / Product Manager: decides what to build and prioritises the backlog. Tools for all: JIRA, Confluence, MS Project.

items.q: What skills should a UI/UX designer have?
items.a: UI/UX designer skills: Figma (main tool), Adobe XD / Sketch, wireframing and prototyping, user research and usability testing, information architecture, design systems, responsive and mobile design, basic HTML / CSS understanding. Always ask for a portfolio (Behance, Dribbble or a personal site) and their role in each project.

items.q: What skills should a Salesforce developer have?
items.a: Salesforce roles: Admin (configuration, users, profiles, flows, reports), Developer (Apex, SOQL, Lightning Web Components, Visualforce, triggers, integrations via REST / SOAP), Consultant / Architect (solution design). Clouds: Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud, Experience Cloud. Certifications matter a lot: Administrator, Platform Developer I / II.

items.q: What are SAP modules?
items.a: SAP is enterprise (ERP) software. Common modules: FICO (finance and controlling), MM (materials management), SD (sales and distribution), PP (production planning), HCM / SuccessFactors (HR), ABAP (SAP programming), BASIS (technical administration), SAP S/4HANA (the latest version). Hiring tip: confirm module, implementation vs support experience, number of full-cycle implementations, and S/4HANA experience.

items.q: What skills does a cyber security engineer need?
items.a: Cyber security roles and skills: SOC analyst (SIEM tools like Splunk, QRadar, Sentinel; incident monitoring), VAPT / penetration tester (Burp Suite, Nmap, Metasploit, OWASP Top 10), network security (firewalls, IDS / IPS), cloud security, IAM. Certifications: CEH, OSCP, CompTIA Security+, CISSP (senior), CISM.

items.q: What skills does a system or network admin need?
items.a: System administrator: Windows Server, Active Directory, Linux, virtualisation (VMware, Hyper-V), backups, Microsoft 365 / Exchange, patching, scripting (PowerShell, Bash). Network engineer: routing and switching (CCNA / CCNP), firewalls (Fortinet, Palo Alto, Cisco), VPN, LAN / WAN, wireless. IT support / desktop support: hardware and OS troubleshooting, ticketing tools (ServiceNow), customer handling.

items.q: What are the experience levels for tech roles?
items.a: Typical tech experience levels: Fresher / Trainee (0 to 1 year), Junior / Software Engineer / SDE-1 (1 to 3 years), Senior Software Engineer / SDE-2 (3 to 6 years), Lead / Tech Lead / SDE-3 (6 to 10 years), Architect / Principal Engineer / Engineering Manager (10+ years). Titles differ by company; match on responsibilities and skills, not just title.

items.q: What is an API?
items.a: An API (Application Programming Interface) is a way for two software systems to talk to each other. Example: a mobile app asks the server for a user's orders through an API. REST API is the most common style (uses URLs and HTTP methods like GET, POST); GraphQL is another style. When a JD says "REST API development", the developer should have built such APIs on the backend.

items.q: What are microservices?
items.a: Microservices means building an application as many small independent services (e.g. separate services for users, payments, orders), each deployed on its own and talking through APIs or message queues (Kafka, RabbitMQ). The opposite is a monolith (one big application). Microservice experience usually comes with Spring Boot / Node.js, Docker, Kubernetes and cloud.

items.q: What is CI/CD?
items.a: CI/CD = Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery (or Deployment). Every time a developer pushes code, an automated pipeline builds it, runs tests and deploys it. Tools: Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure DevOps, CircleCI. DevOps engineers build these pipelines; developers and QA use them.

items.q: What are Docker and Kubernetes?
items.a: Docker packages an application with everything it needs into a "container", so it runs the same everywhere. Kubernetes (K8s) manages many containers in production: starting, scaling, restarting and load balancing them. Managed Kubernetes services: EKS (AWS), AKS (Azure), GKE (Google). Common in DevOps, cloud and backend JDs.

items.q: What is Agile and Scrum?
items.a: Agile is a way of building software in small increments with frequent feedback. Scrum is the most popular Agile method: work is done in sprints (usually 2 weeks) with a daily stand-up meeting, sprint planning, review and retrospective. Roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, development team. JIRA is the common tool to track stories and bugs.

items.q: What is SDLC and STLC?
items.a: SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle): requirement → design → development → testing → deployment → maintenance. STLC (Software Testing Life Cycle) is the testing part: requirement analysis → test planning → test case design → environment setup → test execution → test closure. QA candidates should explain both clearly.

items.q: What is Git and GitHub?
items.a: Git is a version control tool that tracks code changes and lets many developers work together. GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket are websites that host Git repositories. Almost every developer and automation tester JD needs Git. A candidate's public GitHub profile can show real code samples.

items.q: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases?
items.a: SQL (relational) databases store data in tables with fixed columns and use the SQL language: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server. NoSQL databases store data more flexibly: documents (MongoDB), key-value (Redis), wide-column (Cassandra), graph (Neo4j). Most backend roles need at least one SQL database; MongoDB is common with Node.js.

items.q: What are IaaS, PaaS and SaaS?
items.a: Cloud service models: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service): rent servers, storage and networks (AWS EC2, Azure VMs). PaaS (Platform as a Service): the provider runs the servers, you deploy code (Azure App Service, Heroku, Google App Engine). SaaS (Software as a Service): ready software used over the internet (Gmail, Salesforce, Zoho).

items.q: Give a JD template for a software developer
items.a:
Software developer JD template:
Title: <Senior> <Java / Python / React> Developer
Experience: <3 to 6> years | Location: <City> (<Hybrid / Remote / Onsite>) | Notice: <immediate to 30 days>
About the role: You will design, build and maintain <product / services> with a team of <N> engineers.
Responsibilities: build and maintain <backend APIs / UI features>; write clean, tested code; review code; work with product and QA in Agile sprints; troubleshoot production issues.
Must have: <core language + framework>, <database>, REST APIs, Git, <N>+ years hands-on.
Good to have: <cloud>, Docker / Kubernetes, CI/CD, <domain>.
Compensation: <range> + benefits.

items.q: Give a JD template for a QA automation engineer
items.a:
QA automation engineer JD template:
Title: QA Automation Engineer | Experience: <3 to 5> years | Location: <City / Remote>
Responsibilities: design and maintain automation frameworks for web and API testing; write and run automated and manual test cases; integrate tests in CI/CD; report and track bugs in JIRA; work with developers in Agile sprints.
Must have: Selenium WebDriver with Java (or Cypress / Playwright), TestNG / Cucumber, POM framework design, API testing (Postman, Rest Assured), SQL basics, Git, Jenkins.
Good to have: Appium (mobile), JMeter (performance), cloud test platforms (BrowserStack), ISTQB certification.

items.q: What are red flags in technical candidates?
items.a: Red flags in tech profiles: CV lists many technologies but the candidate can't explain one project in depth; vague answers about their own role ("we did" but never "I did"); experience mostly support / maintenance while claiming development; inconsistent dates or companies that can't be verified; different person or lip-sync issues on video interviews (proxy); reluctance to switch on the camera; very short notice of availability with long notice periods. Use video screening and ask for specific project details to verify.

items.q: Which certifications are valuable for IT candidates?
items.a: Valuable IT certifications: Cloud: AWS Solutions Architect / Developer / DevOps, Azure AZ-104 / AZ-204 / AZ-305, Google Cloud Professional. Kubernetes: CKA, CKAD. Testing: ISTQB. Agile / PM: CSM, PSM, PMP. Security: CEH, OSCP, CISSP. Data: Databricks, Snowflake, Microsoft PL-300 (Power BI). Salesforce: Admin, Platform Developer. Certifications help, but hands-on project experience matters more.
